title: Type-II Error Bounds for Test Supermartingales from Lower-Tail Hypotheses
summary: In safe hypothesis testing with test supermartingals, Ville's inequality provides anytime-valid type-I error guarantees for every significance level $α\in(0,1]$, if one rejects the null hypothesis whenever the wealth process first exceeds $\frac{1}α$. Due to an inherent asymmetry, the type-II error does not have such guarantees: a heavy concentration of the probability on the lower tail of the log-increments can lead to one catastrophic bet that undoes any amount of accumulated evidence.
